blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 41 sold over 5 months against an average of 40.8 listed, about 5.0 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 10 sold. Condos and townhomes: 113 sold over 5 months against an average of 99.6 listed, about 4.4 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was July with 29 sold.

Clayton is in Surrey, not Langley — the City plans it as Clayton Heights, about 809 hectares from Fraser Highway in the south to the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) in the north and west, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east.
The City's plan neighbourhoods inside Clayton Heights are East Clayton, West Clayton and North Clayton, and a land use plan for North Clayton has not yet been initiated.

The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board (FVREB) sub-area is called Clayton, one of three sub-areas of the board community Cloverdale, alongside Cloverdale and Serpentine — board name and City planning name (Clayton Heights) describe the same ground.

Clayton is a post-1999 planned community — East Clayton was endorsed in 2003 as the first urban neighbourhood, and West Clayton's final Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) was approved in July 2015 as the second.
West Clayton is planned as the future home of over 12,000 Surrey residents, with a mixed-use urban centre beside a future rapid transit station at 184 Street and Fraser Highway.
The civic anchor is Clayton Community Centre, 7155 187A Street, a 75,000 square foot facility integrating arts, recreation, library and parks, officially opened October 16, 2021.

Do not rely on an old NCP label alone — the City records that East and West Clayton land use designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) update, so confirm a lot's current OCP designation.

blocks.text: Clayton: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Station proximity is a plan fact, not yet a service — Clayton Station and Hillcrest–184 Street Station are named project stations with an anticipated in-service date of 2029.

The former RF-12 and RF-SD zone names in older Clayton material were replaced by R4 Small Lot Residential and R6 Semi-Detached in Surrey's July 8, 2024 SSMUH changes — older labels are pre-2024 names.

Current bus detail stated in a 2026 City planning report for east Clayton: the closest bus stops are on 72 Avenue at 191 Street, route 370 runs Willowbrook to Cloverdale and route 372 runs Langley Centre to Clayton Heights.

A 10-metre multi-use pathway is required along the south edge of the 74 Avenue townhouse site in that same report, linking east–west to Salmonberry Park — trail connections here arrive through development conditions, lot by lot.

Clayton Hub / West Clayton Blocks 1 and 2 — 18120, 18140, 18160 72 Avenue and 18111, 18139, 18147 Fraser Highway; applicant STX Fraser Development LP / Steelix Builders Group Ltd.; mixed use with one six-storey commercial building, two six-storey residential buildings and one townhouse site; STATUS: planning report June 29, 2026, rezoning application 7926-0132-00, read 2026-11-03.

7147 and 7131 182 Street, West Clayton — six-storey residential building, 144 dwelling units over two levels of underground parking; STATUS: planning report June 29, 2026, application 7924-0066-00 proposing rezoning from Acreage Residential (RA) to Low-Rise Apartment (MR7), read 2026-11-03.
19016, 19044 and 19084 74 Avenue — 97-unit townhouse project over three lots, access from future 73A Avenue; STATUS: planning report July 13, 2026, application 7924-0277-00, read 2026-11-03.
Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5 percent penalty after July 2 and a further 5 percent after September 2.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) applies in Surrey, a designated taxable area.
Clayton's current bus spine is Fraser Highway and 72 Avenue — routes 370 and 372 serve the east Clayton stops at 72 Avenue and 191 Street, per the City's 2026 planning report.
Fraser Highway is also the SkyTrain corridor: the extension runs along Fraser Highway from King George Station to Langley City.
Confirm ALR status on any lot at Clayton's north or west edge before assuming residential rebuild rights — the plan area runs to the ALR on both edges.

Confirm the current OCP designation, not the superseded NCP label, and check whether a lot falls inside a Transit-Oriented Area (TOA) around the future 184 Street or 190 Street stations, which changes the density frame.
Confirm the municipality on title before an offer near the eastern edge — Surrey and Township of Langley rules diverge at that line.

faq.a: Schools confirmed by name and address in the Clayton and east Cloverdale part of Surrey include Katzie Elementary, Hazelgrove Elementary and Clayton Heights Secondary.

faq.q: What is the Clayton Community Centre?
faq.a: It is Clayton's combined recreation, arts and library building at 7155 187A Street. The 75,000 square foot centre officially opened October 16, 2021 and includes a fitness centre, a gymnasium and a full-service 14,000 square foot Surrey Libraries branch, which is why it functions as the neighbourhood's civic centre rather than a single-purpose hall.

faq.q: Is Clayton in Surrey or Langley?
faq.a: Surrey. The page covers the Clayton sub-area of Surrey's Cloverdale community; the City plans the ground as Clayton Heights, approximately 809 hectares from Fraser Highway to the ALR, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east — homes east of that municipal boundary are in the Township, not in Surrey Clayton.

The Surrey Langley SkyTrain project names Hillcrest-184 Street Station and Clayton Station (190 Street and Fraser Highway) among its eight stations, and TransLink states an anticipated in-service date of 2029 for the 16-kilometre Expo Line extension from King George Station to Langley City.
